newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Normandy to list on Canadian exchanges.
newsitem.headline: Normandy to list on Canadian exchanges.

text.p: Gold major Normandy Mining Ltd said on Thursday it intended to to list on both the Toronto and Montreal Stock Exchanges by October this year.
Normandy chairman Robert de Crespigny said most investment in the US$70 billion gold industry was in North America and the company already had a number of U.S. and Canadian shareholders.
"We are not going there to raise capital, we are going there to make our shares more accessible," he told reporters.
He said Normandy should attract international investors because of the comapny's size and performance, and he hoped the listing would be completed by October 1997.
Normandy earlier reported record quarterly gold production of 410,102 ounces for the June quarter and annual production of 1.515 million ounces.
De Crespigny said it was important to note the contribution from zinc and commercial mineral operations, and the initial contribution from the Goldfields natural gas pipeline in Western Australia.
Normandy said its Ovacik mine in Turkey should produce its first gold in December this year, while the Vera Nancy joint venture in Queensland was nearing completion.
De Crespigny said despite the lower gold price, the cash cost of all production was currently below the gold price.
The gold price has fallen below US$320 following the Reserve Bank of Australia's announcement early last Friday it had sold 167 tonnes of gold.
